newsitem.title: USA: Stocks extend rally, Dow hits new high.
newsitem.headline: Stocks extend rally, Dow hits new high.

text.p: Stocks surged on Monday, taking the Dow Jones industrial average to a new high as bulls kept charging after Friday's rally sparked by a low interest rate outlook.
At 1 p.m. EDT 1700 GMT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up about 47.56 points, or 0.64 percent, to 7,483.34. Earlier, the blue-chip index hit a high of 7,511.53.
In the broader market, advancing issues outpaced declines by a 13-9 margin on volume of 263 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index rose 10.72 points to 1,415.56.
Analysts said they expected investors to take profits, especially as the dollar and bond market were weaker.
"We're looking for the market to consolidate Friday's and Monday's gains," said Dan Ascani, president and director of research at Global Market Strategists Inc.
Tom Carpenter, a managing director and chief economist at ASB Capital Management Inc., said the morning gain was "well enough at this point."
"We had a good few days from Friday but we've had some deterioration in the long bond," Carpenter said.

The bond market weakened after the U.S. Treasury said it would cancel sales of conventional 10-year notes in July and October. The 30-year U.S. Treasury bond fell 13/32, raising its yield to 6.81 percent from 6.80 percent at Friday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Ascani said the dollar, brought down by European monetary union concerns and U.S. protests at swelling Japanese trade surpluses, has also made investors wary of buying U.S. stocks.
The dollar fell to 1.7035 German marks from 1.7275 marks late Friday, and slid to 112.64 Japanese yen from 114.23 yen.
"When the dollar is this weak, investors kind of pause. The market is a little bit worried about it," Ascani said.
Despite expected profit-taking, analysts see the market holding firm because of a dearth of negative news and a feeling that the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates when it meets in July.
"I think the fundamentals for the equities market are excellent this year," Carpenter said. "This is something that happens once in every 50 years."
Bill Allyn, a head trader at Jeffries & Co., said, "There just isn't any bad economic news. Until some competition to the stock market is introduced, we are going to see this."

Cable company stocks jumped after Microsoft Corp. said it would invest about $1 billion in cable operator Comcast Corp. Microsoft shares gained 7/16 to 124-1/2 while Comcast surged 3-7/16 to 21-11/16.

Also, Cablevision Systems Corp. said it would buy 10 cable television systems in the New York area from cable giant Tele-Communications Inc. Cablevision gained 8-1/8 to 42-3/4 while TCI rose 1-1/16 to 16-1/8.
Safeco Corp. agreed to buy American States Financial Corp. for about $2.8 billion in a deal that would make Safeco the 12th-largest property casualty insurer in the United States.
Safeco slipped about 3/4 to 44-1/2, while American States Financial climbed 7-1/4 to 45-3/8.
